Decision-weighted scores for survival predictions

Source: R/dwscore.R
dwscore.Rd

Scores predicted risks at one or more horizons with a decision-weighted proper score: the loss of the rule "act if predicted risk exceeds c", averaged over thresholds c with a weight w(c). The weight states which risk thresholds matter. Every such score equals a weighted area under the net benefit curve, with weight (1 - c) w(c), so a threshold range restricts model comparison to the decisions clinicians actually make.

Usage

dwscore(
  object,
  y,
  times = NULL,
  weight = c("range", "survacc", "brier", "log", "beta"),
  thresholds = c(0.05, 0.2),
  shape = c(2, 18)
)

Arguments

object

A numeric matrix of survival probabilities (rows = subjects, columns = times), for example from predict().

y

A survival::Surv() object with one entry per row of object.

times

Evaluation times. NULL reads the "times" attribute or column names of the form "t=<time>".

weight

Threshold weight:

"range"

uniform on thresholds (default); only decisions with a threshold in that range count.

"survacc"

spherical weight \((c^2 + (1 - c)^2)^{-3/2}\); the loss is 1 - SurvAcc.

"brier"

constant weight 2; the loss is the Brier score.

"log"

weight \(1 / (c (1 - c))\); the loss is the logarithmic score.

"beta"

Beta density with parameters shape.

thresholds

Length-2 numeric range c(lower, upper) in [0, 1] for weight = "range" (default c(0.05, 0.20)).

shape

Length-2 numeric Beta parameters for weight = "beta" (default c(2, 18), mean threshold 0.10).

Value

A data frame with columns time, weight and loss (lower is better for every weight).

Details

With risk \(r = 1 - S(t \mid X)\) and event status \(D = I(T \le t)\), the loss is \(L_w(r, 0) = \int_0^r w(c)\, c\, dc\) for a subject event free at t and \(L_w(r, 1) = \int_r^1 w(c) (1 - c)\, dc\) for a subject with an event by t. Right censoring is handled by inverse probability of censoring weights from the Kaplan-Meier estimate of the censoring distribution: subjects event free at t are weighted by \(1 / G(t)\), subjects with an observed event at \(U \le t\) by \(1 / G(U-)\), and subjects censored before t get weight zero. This assumes censoring is independent of the covariates. Range and Beta weights integrate to one, so those losses lie on the scale of an average regret per decision.

In evaluate(), compare() and tune(), use the metric ids "survacc" (SurvAcc, higher is better) and "range:<lower>-<upper>", for example "range:0.05-0.20" (loss, lower is better). Both need a single time.

Examples

m <- fit(Surv(time, status) ~ age + karno, veteran[1:100, ], "coxph")
S <- predict(m, veteran[-(1:100), ], times = c(90, 180))
y <- Surv(veteran$time[-(1:100)], veteran$status[-(1:100)])
dwscore(S, y)
#>   time          weight       loss
#> 1   90 range(0.05,0.2) 0.03659910
#> 2  180 range(0.05,0.2) 0.01463964
dwscore(S, y, weight = "brier")
#>   time weight       loss
#> 1   90  brier 0.17983192
#> 2  180  brier 0.09568638
dwscore(S, y, weight = "range", thresholds = c(0.10, 0.30))
#>   time         weight       loss
#> 1   90 range(0.1,0.3) 0.05502598
#> 2  180 range(0.1,0.3) 0.02342342

# the same scores inside the verbs (single time)
S180 <- predict(m, veteran[-(1:100), ], times = 180)
evaluate(S180, y = y, metrics = c("brier", "survacc", "range:0.05-0.20"))
#> <survalis_eval> model = supplied predictions
#>   scored once on 37 subjects (no resampling)
#>   grid: 1 times in [180, 180]
#>   brier           0.0957
#>   survacc         0.8976
#>   range:0.05-0.20 0.0146
